decisionsTitle: «Sarcini» and «Costuri» say what is actually due
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-11-01:** «What else do you think we need?» — and, after reading a verified review of BR-V3.98-2026-10-31, «Do them all». **The review's four findings** on what «Sarcini» and «Costuri» tell the club: nothing on `/admin/tasks` reminded the club to set «Startul cursei» or «Categorii de vârstă» for a coming race; the page kept asking «Luăm o lună de Mailgun plătit înainte de prima cursă adevărată?» although the club has paid Mailgun since 2026-10-01; «Costuri» on Hobby measured build minutes against a 6 000 that Vercel's pages do not confirm and did not show the Active CPU whose overrun pauses the site; and two sentences said Vercel goes back to Hobby after the race, against §803's rule.

**Decision, the race-day rows.** Two new rows, `raceGunTime` and `raceAgeBands`, one pair per race, read from the live system by `diagnostics/race-day-settings.ts#readRaceDaySettings`: a **published, dated race that takes results** (`eventTakesResults`) starting from six hours ago to three weeks ahead. `events.race_starts_at` is the gun the finish clock counts from (`raceStartsAt ?? startsAt`, §808's `gunOf`), and the event's own start is the gathering time (the editor's help: «Pentru o cursă, aceasta este ora de întâlnire»); `events.result_age_bands` holds the race's categories (§850), and changing them after results are entered ranks the places again, so the time to choose is before the race. Each row is `open` while its column is null and `done` once it holds a value, with «Cum» steps in both languages naming the editor's boxes («Când și unde» → «Data și ora» → «Startul cursei»; «Clasament» → «Categorii de vârstă» → «Salvează categoriile»); with no such race in the window there is no row. A cancelled race (`eventStatus` not `SCHEDULED`) draws no row, and a cancelled or date-to-be-announced race never counts as «a race has run». The category row stays open until the club writes its own list: an empty box is the platform's bands (null), and the row asks the question rather than assuming the answer. Because typing the standard bands stores nothing (`setResultAgeBands` sees no change), the copy says so: if the standard categories suit the race there is nothing to do and the row goes by itself a few hours after the start (`RACE_DAY_SETTINGS_GRACE_HOURS`, six), the one phrase both its sentences use in both languages.

**Decision, the Mailgun question.** `moneyDecisions` no longer hard-codes `mailgunBeforeRace` as open. It is derived from the club's own «Planul Mailgun» setting (`readEmailPlan`): any plan but Free answers it (a typed `CUSTOM` plan too), and so does a published or archived race that has already started (`aRaceHasRun`): archiving a race that ran does not reopen the question. It is open only while the plan is Free and no race has run.

**Decision, «Costuri» on Hobby.** The Vercel line on Hobby is measured by **Active CPU against Hobby's 4 hours** (`VERCEL_HOBBY_ACTIVE_CPU_HOURS_PER_MONTH`), read from the very billing reading `/devs` shows (`readVercelUsageCached`), projected to the month's end like the other lines, with its own over-the-limit sentence (Vercel can pause the site for about thirty days). The build minutes are no longer presented as a limit: their 6 000 ceiling is gone from the line, `MonthCostFacts` and the page. Pro is unchanged, its «not measured» line keeps naming both variables (`unmeasured.vercelPro`) (the seats' price, the build minutes counted against no ceiling), and the usage billing is not even asked for on Pro. A usage line Vercel gives in a unit that is not an hour is «not measured» with its reason, never compared with the four.

**Decision, the wording.** `Admin.tasks.nextSpend.none` and `vercelMore`, in both languages, state §803's rule: Vercel goes back to Hobby only after two months in a row under 3 Active CPU-hours, never on a date and never «after the race». The rule is Vercel's alone, so `nextSpend.none` names Vercel only: Mailgun's way back to Free is its own guide's step («După cursă: anulezi în Mailgun, apoi aici pui Free la loc»), and a sentence saying «what is paid stays» would contradict it. The row «Consumul Vercel în cifre, pe /devs» (`vercelUsage`) speaks of the same Active CPU against Hobby's 4 hours, with the warning `/devs` gives at 80 %, and of no build-minute ceiling, so no sentence on any screen still presents the unconfirmed 6 000 as a limit. In `docs/PLATFORM.md` two lines follow: the Vercel row of «What each service gives away» says Hobby comes back only by that rule, never «after the race», and the note on `/devs`' Vercel card says no screen reads `VERCEL_HOBBY_BUILD_MINUTES_PER_MONTH` any more.

**Refused.** A single "race day" row listing every missing setting (the club closes one box at a time and each has its own screen); a window of the whole season (a row for a race in March in November is noise); making the category row green on the platform's default (it would answer a question nobody asked); keeping the unconfirmed 6 000 as a softer «estimate» (a figure shown against a ceiling reads as a limit whatever its label); reading Active CPU a second way for «Costuri» (one number, one source, two screens); saying in `nextSpend.none` when Mailgun goes back to Free (its guide says it, and the «Costuri» sentence is about Vercel's rule).
changelogLine: - **«Sarcini» reminds the club of «Startul cursei» and «Categorii de vârstă», and «Costuri» measures Hobby by Active CPU** — two race-day rows read from the live system, the Mailgun question follows the club's own plan, Hobby is shown against 4 Active CPU-hours instead of an unconfirmed build-minute ceiling (on «Costuri» and in the «Sarcini» row for `/devs`), and the Vercel wording states the two-months-under-3-hours rule. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given a published, dated race that takes results and starts from six hours ago to three weeks ahead, when `/admin/tasks` renders, then one row per setting asks for «Startul cursei» and «Categorii de vârstă», `open` while the event's `race_starts_at` / `result_age_bands` is empty and `done` once set, each with «Cum» steps in both languages; with no such race there is no row (2026-11-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN). Verification: integration `diagnostics/race-day-settings.test.ts`; unit `diagnostics/owner-tasks.test.ts`.

Given the club's «Planul Mailgun» setting, when `/admin/tasks` renders, then the question «Luăm o lună de Mailgun plătit înainte de prima cursă adevărată?» is open only while the plan is Free and no published or archived race has started, and answered on any paid plan (2026-11-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN). Verification: unit `diagnostics/platform-plans.test.ts`; integration `diagnostics/race-day-settings.test.ts`.

Given the Costuri sentences about Vercel's next spend, when they render in either language, then they state that Vercel goes back to Hobby after two months under 3 Active CPU-hours and never after the race, and the sentence for no next spend says nothing of Mailgun (2026-11-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN). Verification: unit `diagnostics/platform-plans.test.ts`.

Given the Vercel plan is Hobby, when «Setări» → «Costuri» renders the Vercel line, then it measures the month's Active CPU against Hobby's 4 hours, from the reading `/devs` shows, and presents no build-minute ceiling; on Pro the line is unchanged (2026-11-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN). Verification: unit `diagnostics/month-costs.test.ts`, `diagnostics/month-costs-read.test.ts`.

Given the «Sarcini» row «Consumul Vercel în cifre, pe /devs», when it renders open or done in either language, then it names the Active CPU against Hobby's 4 hours and no build-minute ceiling (2026-11-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN). Verification: unit `diagnostics/owner-tasks.test.ts`.

batchLine: «Sarcini» asks for the gun time and age categories, the Mailgun question follows the plan, «Costuri» reads Hobby by Active CPU
